subtitle: Let people book you, no sign-up for them
description:
Share one link and let people book time with you. Your page lives at your own address, like /@avery, with your photo, what you do, your website and profiles, and a link for each kind of meeting you offer, each showing the next time that's open. No account for them, no app, no back-and-forth.

Your free time lies on a strip of days, time running left to right like a video editor's timeline. Guests tap a shaded span and the meeting drops in, the length of the event; they drag it along the day and it snaps to the times that are open. If nothing suits them, they paint when they're free instead, even outside your hours, and where it meets your free time it glows. You see their times over your own week, drag the meeting to a time inside them and accept, or say no with a note.

Both of you get an email with Add to Calendar buttons for Google, Apple and Outlook. The guest can move or cancel with the link in their email. Paint your weekly hours on the same kind of strip, trimming and sliding spans like clips, even onto another day, where they trade places with what's in the way; drag a day over another and the two swap as you go. Pause a day with a switch, zoom the day in and out, and keep days off. Guests see times in their own zone, with daylight saving handled on both sides.

Insights show page views, visitors, profile clicks, bookings, time on page, where visitors came from, what they used and where they are, without cookies. Tracked links tag your page for a flyer, a newsletter or a talk, each with a QR code, and show which one brought each visit and booking. And you can run all of it from Claude: connect its MCP connector and it can change your profile, hours and event types, list meetings, answer requests and read your insights.
whatsNew: Your profile has a tab of its own in the sidebar and tab bar, with your page as guests see it at the top, and it saves as you type. Drag a day over another and the two swap hours on screen as you go; a span dropped on a full day trades places with what's in its way. Signed out, the home page's booking card plays itself. The Analytics link for admins opens Holm's analytics page again, the avatar menu closes when you tap it again, search sheets keep their height as you type, and a booking page you've opened before starts at the soonest open time again.

screenshots.alt: Booking a 30-minute intro call on a phone: days as rows, time running left to right, Avery's free time shaded, and the meeting dropped in at 5:00 PM with a Next button
Suggesting times: two spans the guest painted, one glowing red where it meets Avery's free time, with a link to book 3:30 PM and a Send button
Avery Chen's page: photo, product designer at Northwind, Lisbon with the local time, a welcome note, LinkedIn, X, GitHub and website links, and event types with their next open time
In dark mode, a request from Noah Fischer: his painted times over Avery's hours, the meeting dragged to Monday at 3:00 PM where both are free, and an Accept button

Availability as a week of tracks: weekday spans from 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM painted red with handles to trim them, a switch beside each day with Friday paused and its hours kept, zoom controls, and the time zone below
Insights: tracked links, each with its visitors, QR scans and bookings, a New link button, and where visitors came from below
The host's bookings: the next meeting in an hour, today's meetings, and a Requests tab with two waiting
